content.text:
# 1. Platform Comparison: 8 Major Podcast Hosting & Distribution Options

Each platform was reviewed directly on its live official public pages.

---

### 1. Spotify for Creators (formerly Anchor / Spotify for Podcasters)
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can launch a brand-new show or import/switch an existing show from another host via RSS feed and set up a 301 redirect. You can also claim a show hosted elsewhere.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to Spotify is automatic and native. For third-party apps (Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Overcast, Pocket Casts, etc.), an open RSS feed is provided in your show settings (`Settings > Availability`) for manual submission to directory aggregators.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. Direct video uploads and publishing are natively supported on Spotify (via web, mobile, or Riverside integration). On non-Spotify podcast apps via RSS, video episodes are automatically delivered as audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**: 100% Free ("Completely free podcast hosting in three easy steps", "Host for free, distribute everywhere"). No paid subscription tiers exist on Spotify for Creators (enterprise publishing is managed separately via Spotify Megaphone).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Overview, Audience demographics, Discovery/Impression analytics (where on Spotify you are being discovered), Episode and Video drop-off/retention analytics, and link sharing/referral data. Data export is supported.
  - *Monetization*: Spotify Partner Program (ad revenue share across audio and video; video ad revenue when Spotify Premium members stream video uninterrupted in select markets), Podcast Subscriptions (subscriber-only episodes/content), and sponsorships.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: No automated direct ingest or sync from a YouTube channel. You must manually extract or export audio/video files from your YouTube productions or edit via Riverside to upload. Furthermore, full video playback is exclusive to Spotify’s apps/web player; listeners on Apple Podcasts or other RSS directories receive audio only.

---

### 2. Podbean
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Podbean provides a native show setup wizard as well as an automated RSS feed import tool to migrate existing episodes, metadata, and media files from another host.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Features 1-click distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, iHeartRadio, and PlayerFM, plus a standard open RSS feed.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Unlimited Plus" plan ($29/mo billed annually or $39/mo billed monthly) and higher plans (includes 10 GB uploads/mo, approx. 10 hours of video). The Free and Unlimited Audio plans are strictly audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: Basic Free plan available ($0, includes 5 hours of total audio storage, 100 GB monthly bandwidth, and basic stats).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Unlimited Audio" at $12/month billed annually ($17/month billed monthly), offering unlimited storage, unmetered bandwidth, and 1 GB upload/month (~16 hours of audio).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-compliant podcast stats, user retention trends, geographic insights, and top episode charts.
  - *Monetization*: Podbean Ads Marketplace, Apple Podcasts Subscriptions integration, Patron program (recurring monthly listener funding), and integrated podcast store/paid content.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Podbean features an automated tool to publish audio *to* YouTube (creating an audiogram video), but it does not import or pull content *from* YouTube into your podcast feed. Creators repurposing YouTube videos must strip the audio locally or render MP3s manually. Video hosting requires the more expensive $29/mo tier.

---

### 3. Buzzsprout
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can start a new show from scratch or use Buzzsprout's automated RSS migration tool to transfer episodes and show artwork from an existing host.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Direct automated listings in Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, Castbox, and Google/YouTube Podcasts via an open RSS feed.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Audio + Video" tier ($25/mo billed annually or $30/mo billed monthly) supporting 1080p video resolution and video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube. Audio plans do not support video.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: Free plan includes 2 hours of upload per month, but episodes are hosted for only 90 days (after which they expire), and it does not include video distribution or monetization add-ons.
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: Single Audio plan at $15/month billed annually ($18/month billed monthly) for up to 6 hours of upload per month (72 hrs/year) and unlimited episode retention.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-certified advanced statistics (listener locations, podcast apps used, device breakdown, algorithmic estimates of total listeners per episode).
  - *Monetization*: Buzzsprout Ads (dynamic mid-roll network ads), Subscriptions, Listener Support integration (buy-me-a-coffee / Patreon links), and Visual Soundbites for social promotion.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Upload limits are strictly metered by hours per month (6 hrs/mo on the base paid plan, $3 per extra hour). If you have an extensive back-catalog of past YouTube videos to upload as audio episodes, you will rapidly exceed monthly hour quotas. Ingestion from YouTube is not automatic; files must be uploaded manually.

---

### 4. Transistor.fm
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Transistor allows you to create unlimited separate podcasts under one account or import existing shows from other hosts via RSS feed with automated 301 redirect management.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Provides 1-click distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and YouTube Music via standard RSS.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. Transistor is an Apple-approved hosting partner for HLS video podcasts and supports video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube Music (currently in gradual rollout / beta).
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (offers a 14-day free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Starter" plan at $19/month ($190/year billed annually, equivalent to ~$15.83/month). Includes unlimited podcasts, unlimited episode uploads/storage, and up to 20,000 monthly downloads.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-certified analytics (downloads over time, episode performance comparisons, top listening apps, listener country/city geolocation).
  - *Monetization*: Dynamic ad insertion (pre-roll, mid-roll, post-roll) available on the $49/mo Professional plan; private podcast subscriber feeds; integrated player subscriptions/donation links.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Ingestion is not automated from YouTube. The built-in "Auto-post to YouTube" feature generates static-image video for YouTube from your audio podcast, but it is locked behind the $49/month Professional plan. Repurposing YouTube video back into podcast audio requires you to extract MP3s yourself.

---

### 5. Captivate.fm
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Unlimited shows can be created on any plan, and existing shows can be imported in seconds using Captivate's import tool and RSS redirect guides.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, and all major directories via standard RSS.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Not supported. Captivate is an audio-only podcast hosting platform.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (offers a 30-day free trial). Captivate publicly notes: "Nope! We’re a podcast host for the serious creator."
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Personal" plan at $17/month billed annually ($19/month billed monthly) for up to 30,000 monthly downloads and unlimited shows/episodes.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Advanced IAB-certified analytics, listener drop-off tracking, device and demographic reports, single-promotional link analytics.
  - *Monetization*: Dynamic audio insertion engine (AMIE) for ads and sponsors, Tips and Subscriptions integration, Captivate Memberships, and free access to "Podcast Growth Labs".
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Completely audio-only (no video hosting). To use existing YouTube content, you must extract the audio track yourself. While Captivate can push audio episodes out as videos to YouTube via its integration, it cannot pull from YouTube.

---

### 6. Castos
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Unlimited podcasts and episodes on all plans, with a 1-click RSS migration process for moving an existing show.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Automated syndication to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, and all podcast aggregators.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Pro" plan ($99/month), which includes full video file hosting. The "Growth" plan ($49/month) includes automated video republishing to YouTube. The base "Essentials" plan ($19/month) is audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (14-day free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Essentials" at $19/month billed monthly (or 2 months free when billed annually at $190/year, ~$15.83/mo). Includes unlimited podcasts, unlimited downloads, and unlimited episodes.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: In-depth listener analytics, geographic listening trends, device/app breakdown, and custom PDF exportable reports.
  - *Monetization*: Castos Commerce (direct listener support, paid subscriber private feeds), Castos Dynamic Ads, and automatic episode transcription.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Video file hosting is expensive ($99/mo Pro plan). Although Castos features a dedicated YouTube integration, it operates in reverse: it takes your podcast episode and republishes it *to* YouTube (requires the $49/mo plan). It does not automatically ingest your existing YouTube videos into podcast episodes.

---

### 7. Libsyn
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can set up a new show or import an existing show via RSS feed using Libsyn's migration service.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Global distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, iHeartRadio, and all podcast directories. (Note: Spotify Video distribution is restricted to the $25/mo plan and up).
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. All standard plans include video uploads up to 100 GB/month (~50 hours). However, the $12/month Basic plan only distributes video to YouTube; distributing video directly to Spotify requires the $25/month Advanced plan.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (first 30 days free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: Mentions an "$8 Plan for the bare essentials" on their pricing page; standard entry plan is "Basic" at $12/month (includes 3 hours of audio uploads/month and 100 GB video uploads, but excludes Spotify video distribution).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Basic or Advanced IAB-verified statistics (geographic tracking, episode downloads, listening clients).
  - *Monetization*: Libsyn Ads marketplace (host-read and programmatic ads), Glow.fm subscriptions/memberships, and custom listener tips.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Audio uploads are constrained by strict monthly time allotments (3 hrs/month on the $12 plan; 10 hrs/month on the $25 plan). If you have existing 30-to-60 minute YouTube episodes, back-catalog conversion will quickly stall under these caps. Also, Spotify video distribution is blocked on the cheapest $12 tier.

---

### 8. Acast
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Creators can create a new show or import an existing podcast via RSS feed using Acast’s migration tool.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to every podcast directory including Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, and Pocket Casts.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the dedicated "Video" plan ($39.99/month), which supports video podcast distribution to Apple Podcasts, automatic video-to-audio conversion, and 10,000 monthly video views.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: "Starter" plan is Free ($0), but it is restricted to 1 show and a lifetime limit of 5 episodes unless you opt your show into Acast's advertising marketplace (which unlocks unlimited episodes).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Essential" plan at $14.99/month (unlimited episodes, multiple shows, and ad/sponsorship tools).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Advanced IAB-certified podcast analytics, listener demographics, and performance tracking.
  - *Monetization*: Acast Marketplace (programmatic dynamic ads), sponsorships, and Acast+ (premium subscriber feeds and memberships).
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: The free plan restricts you to 5 episodes unless you grant Acast commercial rights to run ads on your show. Video podcasting requires the $39.99/mo plan. No direct channel scraper or automatic YouTube ingest is offered.

---

# 2. Spotify for Creators: Current Onboarding Path & Guidance

Direct inspection of Spotify for Creators (`creators.spotify.com`) and Spotify Support documentation confirmed the following:

### Live Entry Point for Adding a Podcast
1. **Public Entry Point**:
   - The primary call to action across `creators.spotify.com` is **"Get started"** or **"Sign up"** (both routing through `creators.spotify.com/api/shell/gateway`).
   - On the podcast features page (`creators.spotify.com/features/podcast`), Spotify provides two distinct live entry points:
     - **"Set up a new show"** (links via `creator.spoti.fi/QV6T9IKqiVb`)
     - **"Grow my show on Spotify"** (links via `creator.spoti.fi/6usY4wMqiVb`)
2. **In-Dashboard Entry Point (The "Add your podcast" equivalent)**:
   - Once logged into `creators.spotify.com` with any Spotify account, the direct control to add or link a podcast is located by clicking your **Avatar / Profile icon** in the top-right corner (or the 3-line navigation menu on mobile) and choosing **"Add a new show"**.

### Spotify’s Public Guidance: Creating a New Show vs. Importing by RSS
In its official documentation (*"Adding a new show to your Spotify for Creators account"* and *"Claiming your podcast on Spotify for Creators"*), Spotify distinguishes two distinct paths:

1. **"Create a new show" (Hosting with Spotify)**:
   - *When to choose*: If you are launching a brand-new podcast or if you want to bring existing video/audio from other platforms directly into Spotify’s free hosting environment.
   - *Workflow*: You create the show inside Spotify for Creators, upload audio or video files directly (or use their Riverside.fm integration), and publish. Episodes automatically appear on Spotify. Spotify generates an open RSS feed (`Settings > Availability`) that you can copy and submit manually to other directories (Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, etc.).
2. **"Find an existing show" (Hosting Elsewhere / Claiming via RSS)**:
   - *When to choose*: If your podcast is already hosted on an independent host (such as Buzzsprout, Podbean, Transistor, or Libsyn) and you want access to Spotify’s creator dashboard without moving your media files.
   - *Workflow*: You select **"Find an existing show" > "Somewhere else"**, paste your podcast's public RSS feed or Spotify show URL, and enter an 8-digit verification code emailed to the address listed in your RSS feed. This "claims" your show, giving you access to Spotify's audience analytics, retention curves, Q&A/polls, and the ability to upload Spotify-exclusive video episodes to replace existing audio episodes—while keeping your existing host as the source of truth.
3. **"Switching / 301 Redirect"**:
   - Spotify provides a dedicated switch tool (`creators.spotify.com/switch`) for podcasters who want to transfer their entire show from another host to Spotify for Creators. You paste your RSS feed, Spotify imports all existing episodes and metadata into their hosting, and you apply a 301 redirect on your old host to maintain all existing subscribers on all platforms without starting over.

---

# 3. Recommendation for a YouTube-First Creator

### Best Low-Cost Path to Repurpose YouTube to Audio Without Getting Boxed In
If you already produce a show on YouTube and want to transition to audio podcasting now with Spotify as a priority—without spending unnecessary money and without locking yourself in:

1. **Extract Audio Locally**: Since no major podcast host automatically pulls and converts full YouTube video back-catalogs for free, use a standard workflow (exporting the master audio track as an MP3/WAV from your editing timeline, or batch-extracting audio from your finished YouTube videos).
2. **Host on Spotify for Creators (`creators.spotify.com`) as your Launch Pad**:
   - **Cost**: **$0 / month** (completely free hosting, unlimited storage, unlimited episodes).
   - **Spotify Benefits**: Native Spotify publishing, instant eligibility for Spotify’s Partner Program, audience retention graphs, and comment/poll engagement.
   - **Avoiding Lock-In**: Spotify for Creators provides a standard, compliant RSS feed under `Settings > Availability`. You submit this RSS feed once to Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, and Overcast. If you ever outgrow Spotify for Creators or want advanced third-party ad insertion tools, Spotify fully supports standard **301 redirects** (`Settings > Update RSS feed / Switch away from Spotify for Creators`), allowing you to migrate your subscribers to any host (like Transistor or Podbean) with zero audience loss.
   - **Video Option Ready**: Whenever you decide to publish video to Spotify, you can upload video files directly to Spotify for Creators at no extra charge.

# 4. Why the Top 2 Options Beat the Rest

The two clear winners for a YouTube-first creator looking for a low-cost, unboxed entry point are **Spotify for Creators** and **Podbean** (with **Transistor** as the premier paid alternative).

### Why Spotify for Creators & Podbean Beat the Others:
1. **Cost & Upload Caps**:
   - *Spotify for Creators* is completely free with no episode or hour caps.
   - *Podbean* offers a permanent free tier and an unlimited audio storage plan for just $12/month.
   - *Competitors fail here*: Buzzsprout restricts the base plan to only 6 hours of uploads/month ($18/mo) and deletes episodes on its free tier after 90 days. Libsyn meters uploads to 3 hours/month on its $12 plan. Transistor ($19/mo) and Captivate ($19/mo) offer no permanent free tier at all. For a creator with an existing YouTube catalog, hourly upload quotas make back-catalog publishing prohibitively expensive.
2. **Video Flexibility for YouTube Creators**:
   - Because you already produce video for YouTube, you will eventually want video podcasting.
   - *Spotify for Creators* includes free, native video podcast publishing directly to Spotify’s massive audience.

Claiming your podcast on Spotify for Creators

If you host your podcast with Buzzsprout, Voxnest, Podbean, or any host except Spotify, you can claim your show on Spotify for Creators.

A show can only be claimed once on Spotify for Creators. If a podcast you’re trying to claim has already been claimed, you’ll need to reach out to the existing admin or owner of the show in order for them to follow these steps.

New to Spotify for Creators?
Go to creators.spotify.com and log in to any Spotify account.
Note: If you don't have a Spotify account, you can create one for free.
Select Find an existing show then Somewhere else.
Enter your podcast’s RSS feed or Spotify show URL.
Already have access to another podcast?
Log in to creators.spotify.com.
Hit your avatar/the 3 lines in the top-right corner, then Add a new show. On mobile, you need to tap the arrow at the bottom of the screen to see this option.
Select Find an existing show then Somewhere else.
Enter your podcast’s RSS feed or Spotify show URL.
Verifying your ownership

We’ll send a verification code to the email address in your RSS feed.

Copy the 8-digit code and paste it in the submit form.

Tip: If you don’t receive the verification code, try these steps.

Adding team members to a claimed show

If you’ve claimed your podcast on Spotify for Creators, you’re the admin of the claimed show by default. Follow these steps to invite team members to your podcast. You can read more about the levels of access you can provide to a podcast here.

# 1. Platform Comparison: 8 Major Podcast Hosting & Distribution Options

Each platform was reviewed directly on its live official public pages.

---

### 1. Spotify for Creators (formerly Anchor / Spotify for Podcasters)
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can launch a brand-new show or import/switch an existing show from another host via RSS feed and set up a 301 redirect. You can also claim a show hosted elsewhere.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to Spotify is automatic and native. For third-party apps (Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Overcast, Pocket Casts, etc.), an open RSS feed is provided in your show settings (`Settings > Availability`) for manual submission to directory aggregators.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. Direct video uploads and publishing are natively supported on Spotify (via web, mobile, or Riverside integration). On non-Spotify podcast apps via RSS, video episodes are automatically delivered as audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**: 100% Free ("Completely free podcast hosting in three easy steps", "Host for free, distribute everywhere"). No paid subscription tiers exist on Spotify for Creators (enterprise publishing is managed separately via Spotify Megaphone).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Overview, Audience demographics, Discovery/Impression analytics (where on Spotify you are being discovered), Episode and Video drop-off/retention analytics, and link sharing/referral data. Data export is supported.
  - *Monetization*: Spotify Partner Program (ad revenue share across audio and video; video ad revenue when Spotify Premium members stream video uninterrupted in select markets), Podcast Subscriptions (subscriber-only episodes/content), and sponsorships.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: No automated direct ingest or sync from a YouTube channel. You must manually extract or export audio/video files from your YouTube productions or edit via Riverside to upload. Furthermore, full video playback is exclusive to Spotify’s apps/web player; listeners on Apple Podcasts or other RSS directories receive audio only.

---

### 2. Podbean
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Podbean provides a native show setup wizard as well as an automated RSS feed import tool to migrate existing episodes, metadata, and media files from another host.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Features 1-click distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, iHeartRadio, and PlayerFM, plus a standard open RSS feed.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Unlimited Plus" plan ($29/mo billed annually or $39/mo billed monthly) and higher plans (includes 10 GB uploads/mo, approx. 10 hours of video). The Free and Unlimited Audio plans are strictly audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: Basic Free plan available ($0, includes 5 hours of total audio storage, 100 GB monthly bandwidth, and basic stats).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Unlimited Audio" at $12/month billed annually ($17/month billed monthly), offering unlimited storage, unmetered bandwidth, and 1 GB upload/month (~16 hours of audio).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-compliant podcast stats, user retention trends, geographic insights, and top episode charts.
  - *Monetization*: Podbean Ads Marketplace, Apple Podcasts Subscriptions integration, Patron program (recurring monthly listener funding), and integrated podcast store/paid content.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Podbean features an automated tool to publish audio *to* YouTube (creating an audiogram video), but it does not import or pull content *from* YouTube into your podcast feed. Creators repurposing YouTube videos must strip the audio locally or render MP3s manually. Video hosting requires the more expensive $29/mo tier.

---

### 3. Buzzsprout
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can start a new show from scratch or use Buzzsprout's automated RSS migration tool to transfer episodes and show artwork from an existing host.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Direct automated listings in Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, Castbox, and Google/YouTube Podcasts via an open RSS feed.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Audio + Video" tier ($25/mo billed annually or $30/mo billed monthly) supporting 1080p video resolution and video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube. Audio plans do not support video.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: Free plan includes 2 hours of upload per month, but episodes are hosted for only 90 days (after which they expire), and it does not include video distribution or monetization add-ons.
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: Single Audio plan at $15/month billed annually ($18/month billed monthly) for up to 6 hours of upload per month (72 hrs/year) and unlimited episode retention.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-certified advanced statistics (listener locations, podcast apps used, device breakdown, algorithmic estimates of total listeners per episode).
  - *Monetization*: Buzzsprout Ads (dynamic mid-roll network ads), Subscriptions, Listener Support integration (buy-me-a-coffee / Patreon links), and Visual Soundbites for social promotion.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Upload limits are strictly metered by hours per month (6 hrs/mo on the base paid plan, $3 per extra hour). If you have an extensive back-catalog of past YouTube videos to upload as audio episodes, you will rapidly exceed monthly hour quotas. Ingestion from YouTube is not automatic; files must be uploaded manually.

---

### 4. Transistor.fm
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Transistor allows you to create unlimited separate podcasts under one account or import existing shows from other hosts via RSS feed with automated 301 redirect management.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Provides 1-click distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and YouTube Music via standard RSS.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. Transistor is an Apple-approved hosting partner for HLS video podcasts and supports video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube Music (currently in gradual rollout / beta).
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (offers a 14-day free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Starter" plan at $19/month ($190/year billed annually, equivalent to ~$15.83/month). Includes unlimited podcasts, unlimited episode uploads/storage, and up to 20,000 monthly downloads.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: IAB-certified analytics (downloads over time, episode performance comparisons, top listening apps, listener country/city geolocation).
  - *Monetization*: Dynamic ad insertion (pre-roll, mid-roll, post-roll) available on the $49/mo Professional plan; private podcast subscriber feeds; integrated player subscriptions/donation links.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Ingestion is not automated from YouTube. The built-in "Auto-post to YouTube" feature generates static-image video for YouTube from your audio podcast, but it is locked behind the $49/month Professional plan. Repurposing YouTube video back into podcast audio requires you to extract MP3s yourself.

---

### 5. Captivate.fm
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Unlimited shows can be created on any plan, and existing shows can be imported in seconds using Captivate's import tool and RSS redirect guides.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, and all major directories via standard RSS.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Not supported. Captivate is an audio-only podcast hosting platform.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (offers a 30-day free trial). Captivate publicly notes: "Nope! We’re a podcast host for the serious creator."
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Personal" plan at $17/month billed annually ($19/month billed monthly) for up to 30,000 monthly downloads and unlimited shows/episodes.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Advanced IAB-certified analytics, listener drop-off tracking, device and demographic reports, single-promotional link analytics.
  - *Monetization*: Dynamic audio insertion engine (AMIE) for ads and sponsors, Tips and Subscriptions integration, Captivate Memberships, and free access to "Podcast Growth Labs".
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Completely audio-only (no video hosting). To use existing YouTube content, you must extract the audio track yourself. While Captivate can push audio episodes out as videos to YouTube via its integration, it cannot pull from YouTube.

---

### 6. Castos
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Unlimited podcasts and episodes on all plans, with a 1-click RSS migration process for moving an existing show.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Automated syndication to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, and all podcast aggregators.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the "Pro" plan ($99/month), which includes full video file hosting. The "Growth" plan ($49/month) includes automated video republishing to YouTube. The base "Essentials" plan ($19/month) is audio-only.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (14-day free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Essentials" at $19/month billed monthly (or 2 months free when billed annually at $190/year, ~$15.83/mo). Includes unlimited podcasts, unlimited downloads, and unlimited episodes.
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: In-depth listener analytics, geographic listening trends, device/app breakdown, and custom PDF exportable reports.
  - *Monetization*: Castos Commerce (direct listener support, paid subscriber private feeds), Castos Dynamic Ads, and automatic episode transcription.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Video file hosting is expensive ($99/mo Pro plan). Although Castos features a dedicated YouTube integration, it operates in reverse: it takes your podcast episode and republishes it *to* YouTube (requires the $49/mo plan). It does not automatically ingest your existing YouTube videos into podcast episodes.

---

### 7. Libsyn
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. You can set up a new show or import an existing show via RSS feed using Libsyn's migration service.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Global distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, iHeartRadio, and all podcast directories. (Note: Spotify Video distribution is restricted to the $25/mo plan and up).
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported. All standard plans include video uploads up to 100 GB/month (~50 hours). However, the $12/month Basic plan only distributes video to YouTube; distributing video directly to Spotify requires the $25/month Advanced plan.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: No permanent free tier (first 30 days free trial).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: Mentions an "$8 Plan for the bare essentials" on their pricing page; standard entry plan is "Basic" at $12/month (includes 3 hours of audio uploads/month and 100 GB video uploads, but excludes Spotify video distribution).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Basic or Advanced IAB-verified statistics (geographic tracking, episode downloads, listening clients).
  - *Monetization*: Libsyn Ads marketplace (host-read and programmatic ads), Glow.fm subscriptions/memberships, and custom listener tips.
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: Audio uploads are constrained by strict monthly time allotments (3 hrs/month on the $12 plan; 10 hrs/month on the $25 plan). If you have existing 30-to-60 minute YouTube episodes, back-catalog conversion will quickly stall under these caps. Also, Spotify video distribution is blocked on the cheapest $12 tier.

---

### 8. Acast
- **Create New Show or Import Existing**: Both supported. Creators can create a new show or import an existing podcast via RSS feed using Acast’s migration tool.
- **Distribution to Spotify & Other Podcast Apps**: Supported. Distribution to every podcast directory including Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, and Pocket Casts.
- **Video Podcast Support**: Supported on the dedicated "Video" plan ($39.99/month), which supports video podcast distribution to Apple Podcasts, automatic video-to-audio conversion, and 10,000 monthly video views.
- **Publicly Shown Free Tier or Lowest Paid Price**:
  - *Free Tier*: "Starter" plan is Free ($0), but it is restricted to 1 show and a lifetime limit of 5 episodes unless you opt your show into Acast's advertising marketplace (which unlocks unlimited episodes).
  - *Lowest Paid Tier*: "Essential" plan at $14.99/month (unlimited episodes, multiple shows, and ad/sponsorship tools).
- **Advertised Analytics & Monetization**:
  - *Analytics*: Advanced IAB-certified podcast analytics, listener demographics, and performance tracking.
  - *Monetization*: Acast Marketplace (programmatic dynamic ads), sponsorships, and Acast+ (premium subscriber feeds and memberships).
- **YouTube Repurposing Limitations**: The free plan restricts you to 5 episodes unless you grant Acast commercial rights to run ads on your show. Video podcasting requires the $39.99/mo plan. No direct channel scraper or automatic YouTube ingest is offered.

---

# 2. Spotify for Creators: Current Onboarding Path & Guidance

Direct inspection of Spotify for Creators (`creators.spotify.com`) and Spotify Support documentation confirmed the following:

### Live Entry Point for Adding a Podcast
1. **Public Entry Point**:
   - The primary call to action across `creators.spotify.com` is **"Get started"** or **"Sign up"** (both routing through `creators.spotify.com/api/shell/gateway`).
   - On the podcast features page (`creators.spotify.com/features/podcast`), Spotify provides two distinct live entry points:
     - **"Set up a new show"** (links via `creator.spoti.fi/QV6T9IKqiVb`)
     - **"Grow my show on Spotify"** (links via `creator.spoti.fi/6usY4wMqiVb`)
2. **In-Dashboard Entry Point (The "Add your podcast" equivalent)**:
   - Once logged into `creators.spotify.com` with any Spotify account, the direct control to add or link a podcast is located by clicking your **Avatar / Profile icon** in the top-right corner (or the 3-line navigation menu on mobile) and choosing **"Add a new show"**.

### Spotify’s Public Guidance: Creating a New Show vs. Importing by RSS
In its official documentation (*"Adding a new show to your Spotify for Creators account"* and *"Claiming your podcast on Spotify for Creators"*), Spotify distinguishes two distinct paths:

1. **"Create a new show" (Hosting with Spotify)**:
   - *When to choose*: If you are launching a brand-new podcast or if you want to bring existing video/audio from other platforms directly into Spotify’s free hosting environment.
   - *Workflow*: You create the show inside Spotify for Creators, upload audio or video files directly (or use their Riverside.fm integration), and publish. Episodes automatically appear on Spotify. Spotify generates an open RSS feed (`Settings > Availability`) that you can copy and submit manually to other directories (Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, etc.).
2. **"Find an existing show" (Hosting Elsewhere / Claiming via RSS)**:
   - *When to choose*: If your podcast is already hosted on an independent host (such as Buzzsprout, Podbean, Transistor, or Libsyn) and you want access to Spotify’s creator dashboard without moving your media files.
   - *Workflow*: You select **"Find an existing show" > "Somewhere else"**, paste your podcast's public RSS feed or Spotify show URL, and enter an 8-digit verification code emailed to the address listed in your RSS feed. This "claims" your show, giving you access to Spotify's audience analytics, retention curves, Q&A/polls, and the ability to upload Spotify-exclusive video episodes to replace existing audio episodes—while keeping your existing host as the source of truth.
3. **"Switching / 301 Redirect"**:
   - Spotify provides a dedicated switch tool (`creators.spotify.com/switch`) for podcasters who want to transfer their entire show from another host to Spotify for Creators. You paste your RSS feed, Spotify imports all existing episodes and metadata into their hosting, and you apply a 301 redirect on your old host to maintain all existing subscribers on all platforms without starting over.
